title: Quality assurance of discussions with relatives within the hospital
summary: Family members of seriously ill and dying hospital patients are also affected by the illness and suffering involved. They often face multiple burdens, feel overwhelmed by the situation, and experience significant fear and anxiety. Family members are sometimes involved in medical treatment decisions—particularly when patients are no longer responsive or lack the cognitive capacity to speak for themselves—which can be emotionally distressing. Open communication with the ill person or within the family can sometimes be difficult, and misunderstandings or conflicts may arise. Research has shown that witnessing a significant person suffer from a serious illness can cause family members to become ill themselves. To provide them with an opportunity to discuss their own well-being, unburden themselves, and address their concerns and questions, family members at the University Hospital Bonn are offered psychosocial counseling sessions with a nursing specialist. These sessions take place promptly within a private, secure hospital setting and are an integral part of the nursing team's systemic approach to patient care. This study aims to evaluate the professional quality of these counseling sessions, focusing on nursing communication characterized by care and helpfulness. Following a counseling session, family members are informed about the opportunity to voluntarily participate in this anonymous study; if they agree, they complete a questionnaire specifically designed for the project. Once a sufficient number of questionnaires have been collected, the data will be analyzed to support quality assurance and the further development of family counseling services.
conditions: Relatives of seriously ill and dying patients at the university hospital

interventions.name: Following a routine psychosocial consultation with family members conducted within the clinical setting, the nursing specialist leading the session provides information about the evaluation project. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Participation in a voluntary, self-initiated consultation for family members held within the hospital.
Exclusion criteria:
If family members are able to participate in a family discussion, there are no exclusion criteria.
